statement: LORD core is Python 3.11+ standard library only; any runtime dependency needs a new ADR
One always-on rule holds the contract; procedures live in skills, roles in agents; AGENTS.md is a pointer, never a copy
Every analysis returns a Report of Findings with explicit confidence (confirmed/inferred/unknown); unsupported input is unknown, never an empty result
Bump INDEX_VERSION whenever an extractor's output changes; cached extractions are reused by content hash and would otherwise stay stale
On Windows, Path.write_text without newline='\n' writes CRLF, which makes every line a whitespace-only change in change-surface tests
A PreToolUse hook that exits non-zero or prints malformed JSON denies the tool call; hook code must always print valid JSON and exit 0
Antigravity loads workspace .agents customisations (hooks, rules, skills) only in a trusted workspace; CLI print mode never trusts
evidence: agy changelog: workspace-local hooks ... not loading after trusting a folder

statement: On this machine rg is a Git Bash function, not a binary; Python cannot call ripgrep, so the pure-Python search runs
Antigravity write tools pass TargetFile, TargetContent/ReplacementContent (replace_file_content) and CodeContent/Overwrite (write_to_file); values arrive as strings
python -m pytest runs the full suite in about 2 minutes; verify --run on a clean tree caches per working-tree signature
Hooks have not fired inside a trusted Antigravity session; the launcher working directory (root vs .agents) is unconfirmed and both copies are kept
Google's bundled datacloud_telemetry plugin PreToolUse hook is mis-quoted on Windows and denies every CLI tool call until disabled
evidence: conversation transcript: JSON hook ... failed: exit status 1

statement: Import-based test coverage in verify cannot credit tests that drive code through subprocesses (lord/cli.py, the launchers)

Analyses that compare symbols by name (duplicates, name collisions, tests-for, unknown-receiver calls) stay inside one project root (Inventory.project_root_of); sub-projects of a monorepo legitimately reuse names
verify detects and runs verification steps per sub-project of the changed files (demo: pytest from demo/), falling back to the workspace root
Passing -q to pytest when the project config already sets -q yields -qq and drops the summary line; tooling that parses 'N passed/failed' must not add -q

demo/ is the acceptance environment: reuse traps (normalize_text, format_amount, config constants, validators) and a planted month_bounds defect; oracles live in docs/acceptance/oracles and are excluded from the index by lord.toml
related() scores canonical term keys weighted by rarity across symbol names; reuse thresholds strong 4.5 / weak 2.5 were calibrated on the fixtures and the demo

Live in Antigravity IDE (trusted workspace, Gemini 3.1 Pro High): rules, all five skills and all three hooks load and execute; hooks run with cwd <workspace>/.agents, so .agents/lord_hook.py is the launcher copy in use and the root copy can be dropped

Antigravity IDE Customizations view shows only Rules and Workflows; /hooks, /skills, /agents are CLI slash commands; in the IDE skills appear in the '/' action menu and hooks are proven only by behaviour (hooks.log)

lord context is not counted as pre-edit investigation evidence and is not recorded in the activity log, so the contract's recommended entry point still leads to a gate denial (observed live in T08); minimal fix: add context to INVESTIGATION/TASK_LEVEL commands and record its target
Resemblance detection missed a modified copy of a 16-line validator (exact 0.57, normalised 0.65 vs thresholds 0.70/0.80) in live T04; consider a containment measure for copy-with-edits

On this machine bare 'pytest' resolves to an Anaconda install with a broken langsmith plugin (pydantic_core ImportError); 'python -m pytest' works. Agents that run bare pytest see an environment crash
